title: Blistering Skin Autoimmunity: Split Level, Direct Immunofluorescence and Salt-Split Skin
summary: Separate pemphigus from the pemphigoid diseases by the level of the split and the immunofluorescence pattern: intercellular IgG and a positive Nikolsky sign versus a linear IgG/C3 band, then use 1 mol/L NaCl split skin (roof versus floor) and the serration pattern to tell bullous pemphigoid from epidermolysis bullosa acquisita — and see why an IgG4 food panel diagnoses nothing.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 55 Hits 5 (pemphigus = intraepidermal acantholysis; bullous pemphigoid = subepidermal with linear IgG/C3) and 6 (salt-split skin roof versus floor) and Trap 6 (IgG4 food panels). Checked against Witte 2018, Di Lernia 2020, Mihai 2007, Malik 2021, Koga 2018, Li 2022, Miyamoto 2019, Patterson 2020 and Santos 2017 (all full text via Europe PMC). Qualifications recorded: the roof/floor rule narrows but does not settle the diagnosis (register flag rv-salt-split-roof-floor) and the Nikolsky sign is only moderately sensitive (register flag rv-nikolsky-sensitivity); food-specific IgG/IgG4 has one narrow exception (register flag rv-igg4-food-heiner). Not taught: pemphigus treatment, paraneoplastic pemphigus antigens, dermatitis herpetiformis, the reviewer’s “granular layer” wording for pemphigus foliaceus, and whether large indiscriminate IgE panels are discouraged.

objectives: Separate pemphigus (intraepidermal acantholysis, desmoglein 1 and 3, positive Nikolsky sign) from the pemphigoid diseases (subepidermal split, BP180/BP230, negative Nikolsky sign).
Read direct immunofluorescence on perilesional skin (intercellular versus linear IgG/C3) and state why the linear band alone cannot name the pemphigoid disease.
Use 1 mol/L NaCl split skin (roof versus floor binding) and the serration pattern to distinguish bullous pemphigoid from epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, and state the limits of each test.
Explain why food-specific IgG4 panels have no diagnostic role in food allergy.

scenes.title: Three blistering patients
scenes.altText: Invented scenario. Three patients with blisters: (1) a 58-year-old with painful mouth erosions and flaccid skin blisters, and skin that shears when rubbed; (2) a 79-year-old with intensely itchy tense blisters on urticarial plaques, skin that does not shear; (3) a 45-year-old with blisters over knuckles and knees that heal with milia. Both (2) and (3) show linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane on direct immunofluorescence. Question token: “Which test separates patient 2 from patient 3?”

cues.text: Three patients with blisters. A fifty-eight-year-old has painful mouth erosions and flaccid skin blisters, and rubbing the nearby skin makes the top layer shear away.
A seventy-nine-year-old has intensely itchy tense blisters on red plaques, and rubbing does nothing. A forty-five-year-old blisters over knuckles and knees, healing with tiny milia.
Direct immunofluorescence looks the same in the last two: linear immunoglobulin G and complement along the basement membrane. Which test separates them?

scenes.title: Two levels of split
scenes.altText: Pattern cards (Witte 2018; Di Lernia 2020; Malik 2021; Mihai 2007). Pemphigus diseases: IgG against desmosomal desmogleins (Dsg) 1 and 3 breaks keratinocyte adhesion, giving an INTRAepidermal blister with acantholysis. Pemphigus vulgaris: mucosal-dominant type targets Dsg3; the mucocutaneous type has both anti-Dsg3 and anti-Dsg1. Histology shows separation just above the basal layer, leaving one row of basal keratinocytes on the basement membrane — the “row of tombstones”. Pemphigus foliaceus: Dsg1 only, superficial subcorneal acantholysis, mucous membranes spared. A positive Nikolsky sign (mechanical friction of perilesional skin peels the outermost layer) is common in pemphigus and highly specific, though only moderately sensitive. Pemphigoid diseases: IgG against hemidesmosomal BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 gives a SUBepidermal blister; bullous pemphigoid is mainly diagnosed at ages 75–80 with tense blisters and intense itch, and the Nikolsky sign is negative.

cues.text: Pemphigus antibodies hit desmogleins one and three, the glue between keratinocytes. Adhesion fails inside the epidermis, so the blister is intraepidermal, with acantholysis.

In pemphigus vulgaris the split sits just above the basal layer, leaving one row of basal cells on the basement membrane, the row of tombstones. Mucosal-dominant disease targets desmoglein three; skin involvement adds desmoglein one.

Pemphigus foliaceus targets desmoglein one alone: a shallow subcorneal split, and mucous membranes are spared. Rubbing perilesional skin peels it — a positive Nikolsky sign, highly specific for pemphigus but only moderately sensitive.

Pemphigoid antibodies hit the hemidesmosome instead, BP one eighty, which is collagen seventeen, and BP two thirty. The split is below the epidermis. Bullous pemphigoid is a disease of the mid-seventies to eighties, with tense itchy blisters and a negative Nikolsky sign.

scenes.title: Immunofluorescence: pattern, then plane
scenes.altText: Workflow cards (Witte 2018; Di Lernia 2020; Li 2022; Koga 2018). Step 1 — direct immunofluorescence (DIF) on a perilesional biopsy is the diagnostic gold standard: pemphigus shows intercellular IgG and/or C3 within the epidermis, pemphigoid diseases a linear deposit of IgG and/or C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction. On indirect immunofluorescence, pemphigus sera give the fishnet, chicken-wire pattern on monkey esophagus. DIF is sensitive but not specific: in a 569-patient series its sensitivity was 78.1% and specificity 93.6% for bullous pemphigoid, because every pemphigoid disease deposits linear IgG/C3. Step 2 — indirect immunofluorescence on 1 mol/L NaCl split skin shows which side of the artificial blister the serum binds. ROOF (epidermal side) binders target BP180/BP230: bullous pemphigoid, linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis, anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid. FLOOR (dermal side) binders: epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (type VII collagen), anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 pemphigoid, anti-laminin 332 mucous membrane pemphigoid. Step 3 — serration pattern on DIF: a u-serrated pattern is unique to type VII collagen (epidermolysis bullosa acquisita); n-serration occurs in all other pemphigoid diseases.

cues.text: Step one is direct immunofluorescence on perilesional skin, the gold standard. Pemphigus gives intercellular staining between keratinocytes; pemphigoid diseases give a linear band at the dermal-epidermal junction. Pemphigus serum on monkey esophagus gives the fishnet or chicken-wire pattern.

But that linear band is shared. In one series of five hundred sixty-nine patients, direct immunofluorescence was seventy-eight percent sensitive and ninety-four percent specific for bullous pemphigoid, because every pemphigoid disease deposits linear immunoglobulin G and complement.

Step two splits the skin. Normal skin soaked in one molar sodium chloride separates, and indirect immunofluorescence shows which side the serum binds. Roof binders target BP one eighty and BP two thirty. Floor binders target type seven collagen and other deep antigens.

Step three is the serration pattern of the linear band. Arches closed at the bottom, the u-serrated pattern, are unique to type seven collagen and so to epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Everything else in the pemphigoid group gives n-serration.

scenes.title: Score the three patients
scenes.altText: Decision cards. (1) Mouth erosions, flaccid blisters, positive Nikolsky: pemphigus vulgaris — DIF shows intercellular IgG, and desmoglein ELISA is positive in more than 90% of cases, with titres that generally track extent and activity. (2) Age 79, tense itchy blisters, negative Nikolsky, linear IgG/C3: bullous pemphigoid — serum binds the ROOF of salt-split skin; in a 569-patient series salt-split indirect immunofluorescence was 97.6% sensitive and 99.8% specific and BP180 NC16A ELISA 93.9% sensitive and 95.6% specific, so the two together are the practical pair. (3) Trauma-site blisters healing with milia: epidermolysis bullosa acquisita — serum binds the FLOOR, and DIF shows u-serration. Serology caution: the type VII collagen ELISA has about 45% sensitivity, and combining it with salt-split skin reaches about 50%, so roughly half of these patients are seronegative and a negative result does not exclude the disease.

cues.text: Patient one: mouth erosions, flaccid blisters, positive Nikolsky. Pemphigus vulgaris. Direct immunofluorescence is intercellular, and desmoglein ELISA is positive in over ninety percent, with levels that generally track disease extent.

Patient two: tense blisters at seventy-nine with a negative Nikolsky. Bullous pemphigoid. The serum binds the roof of salt-split skin. In that same series, salt-split indirect immunofluorescence was ninety-eight percent sensitive and nearly one hundred percent specific, and the BP one eighty ELISA ninety-four percent sensitive.
Patient three: blisters at trauma sites healing with milia. The serum binds the floor, and the direct immunofluorescence band shows u-serration. That is epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

One caution on serology. The type seven collagen ELISA is only about forty-five percent sensitive, and even combined with salt-split skin about fifty percent, so roughly half of these patients are seronegative. A negative antibody result does not exclude the disease.

lines: Negative serology does not exclude EBA

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Negative Nikolsky rules out pemphigus” (✓ the sign is highly specific but only moderately sensitive, so a negative sign does not exclude pemphigus); “Roof binding proves bullous pemphigoid, floor binding proves epidermolysis bullosa acquisita” (✓ roof binders also include linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis and anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid; floor binders also include anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 pemphigoid and anti-laminin 332 mucous membrane pemphigoid, so the split side narrows the group and serration pattern or antigen-specific assays finish the job); “An IgG4 food panel diagnoses food allergy” (✓ there is no role for food-specific IgG or IgG4 testing in diagnosing adverse food reactions — IgG to foods is found in essentially all healthy people; diagnosis rests on history, specific IgE or skin-prick testing and oral food challenge).

cues.text: Trap one: a negative Nikolsky sign rules out pemphigus. No. The sign is highly specific but only moderately sensitive, so a negative sign does not exclude it.

Trap two: roof binding proves bullous pemphigoid and floor binding proves epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Not quite. Roof and floor each hold several diseases; the split side narrows the group, and serration pattern or antigen-specific assays finish the job.

Trap three: an immunoglobulin G four food panel diagnoses food allergy. No. There is no role for food-specific immunoglobulin G or G four testing; these antibodies are found in essentially all healthy people. Diagnosis rests on history, specific immunoglobulin E or skin-prick testing, and oral food challenge.

props.title: ✗ “Roof = BP, floor = EBA, done.”
lines: ✓ Several diseases per side · add serration / antigen assay

props.title: ✗ “IgG4 food panel = food allergy.”

cues.text: Memory aid: pemphigus peels in the middle of the epidermis; pemphigoid persists because it splits below it. On the salt-split blister, bullous pemphigoid rides the roof and epidermolysis bullosa acquisita sinks to the floor.

Where it breaks: the roof holds more than bullous pemphigoid and the floor more than epidermolysis bullosa acquisita; a negative Nikolsky sign does not exclude pemphigus; and about half of epidermolysis bullosa acquisita patients are seronegative, so antibody tests alone cannot close the case.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Pemphigus = intraepidermal acantholysis, intercellular IgG, Nikolsky positive · pemphigoid = subepidermal, linear IgG/C3, Nikolsky negative”, “Salt-split skin: roof = BP180/BP230 group · floor = type VII collagen and other deep antigens · u-serration = EBA”.

cues.text: Pemphigus splits inside the epidermis with intercellular immunoglobulin G on direct immunofluorescence while pemphigoid diseases split beneath it with a linear immunoglobulin G and complement band, and salt-split skin plus the serration pattern separates roof-binding bullous pemphigoid from floor-binding epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

props.label: Subepidermal + linear IgG/C3 · roof = BP · floor = EBA (u-serration)

explanation.what: Plain language: in these diseases antibodies attack the glue that holds skin together, and blisters form. Where the glue is attacked decides where the blister forms — inside the top layer of skin, or underneath it. The laboratory stains a skin biopsy to see where the antibodies sit, and can also soak normal skin in strong salt water to split it artificially and see which side of the gap a patient’s serum sticks to. Scientific terms: acantholysis, desmoglein (Dsg) 1 and 3, BP180/collagen XVII, BP230, type VII collagen (COL7), direct immunofluorescence (DIF), indirect immunofluorescence (IIF), 1 mol/L NaCl split skin, n- and u-serration, Nikolsky sign, epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA).
explanation.why: Desmogleins hold keratinocytes to each other inside the epidermis, so antibodies against them cause an intraepidermal split with acantholysis and skin that shears under friction. Hemidesmosomal BP180 and BP230 and the deeper anchoring fibril protein type VII collagen hold the epidermis to the dermis, so antibodies against them cause a subepidermal split with a tense blister roof. Because many antigens sit in that narrow junction, a linear IgG/C3 band is shared by the whole pemphigoid group, and further localisation is needed.
explanation.measure: DIF on perilesional skin is the diagnostic gold standard: intercellular IgG and/or C3 in pemphigus, a linear IgG and/or C3 band at the dermal-epidermal junction in pemphigoid diseases. In one 569-patient series DIF was 78.1% sensitive and 93.6% specific for bullous pemphigoid, salt-split indirect immunofluorescence 97.6% sensitive and 99.8% specific, and BP180 NC16A ELISA 93.9% sensitive and 95.6% specific. Desmoglein ELISA is positive in more than 90% of pemphigus vulgaris. The COL7 ELISA is about 45% sensitive, about 50% combined with salt-split skin. Food-specific IgG or IgG4: no diagnostic role.
explanation.differs: Intraepidermal (pemphigus; Nikolsky positive) versus subepidermal (pemphigoid; Nikolsky negative); suprabasal row of tombstones (pemphigus vulgaris, Dsg3 ± Dsg1, mucosa involved) versus subcorneal superficial split (pemphigus foliaceus, Dsg1, mucosa spared); roof binders (bullous pemphigoid, linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis, anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid) versus floor binders (EBA, anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 pemphigoid, anti-laminin 332 mucous membrane pemphigoid); u-serration (type VII collagen) versus n-serration (all other pemphigoid diseases).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: place the blister from the antigen, read a DIF description, choose salt-split skin to separate bullous pemphigoid from EBA, and reject food IgG4 panels.

mnemonic.text: Pemphigus PEELS in the middle of the epidermis; pemphigoid PERSISTS because it splits below it. On the salt-split blister, BP rides the ROOF and EBA sinks to the FLOOR.
mnemonic.explanation: Ties the level of the split to the Nikolsky sign and the immunofluorescence pattern, then the split side to the two commonest subepidermal diseases.
mnemonic.limitation: The roof holds more than bullous pemphigoid and the floor more than epidermolysis bullosa acquisita; a negative Nikolsky sign does not exclude pemphigus; and about half of epidermolysis bullosa acquisita patients are seronegative, so antibody tests alone cannot close the case.

analogyLimitations: Roof and floor each contain several diseases; the mnemonic keeps only the commonest member of each.
Test performance figures come from referral-centre series and will differ with substrate handling and local populations.
takeaway: Pemphigus splits inside the epidermis with intercellular immunoglobulin G on direct immunofluorescence while pemphigoid diseases split beneath it with a linear immunoglobulin G and complement band, and salt-split skin plus the serration pattern separates roof-binding bullous pemphigoid from floor-binding epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.stem: A biopsy shows acantholysis with separation just above the basal keratinocytes, which remain attached to the basement membrane. Direct immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG within the epidermis. Which finding fits this disease?

options.text: A positive Nikolsky sign, with autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 with or without desmoglein 1
options.rationale: Correct. Suprabasal acantholysis with intercellular IgG is pemphigus vulgaris; a positive Nikolsky sign is common and highly specific for pemphigus, and the targets are Dsg3 (mucosal-dominant) with Dsg1 added in mucocutaneous disease.

options.text: Autoantibodies against BP180 and BP230 with a linear band at the dermal-epidermal junction
options.rationale: Incorrect. Those are pemphigoid targets and give a subepidermal split with a linear band, not intercellular staining.

options.text: Autoantibodies against type VII collagen binding the dermal floor of salt-split skin
options.rationale: Incorrect. Type VII collagen antibodies cause epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, a subepidermal disease with a linear band and floor binding.

options.text: A negative Nikolsky sign with tense blisters in a patient in the late seventies
options.rationale: Incorrect. That is the clinical picture of bullous pemphigoid, where the split is below the epidermis.

questions.stem: Two patients both have a subepidermal blister and linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane on direct immunofluorescence. Indirect immunofluorescence on 1 mol/L NaCl split skin shows that patient A binds the epidermal side and patient B binds the dermal side. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Dermal-side (floor) binding fits epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, but also anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 pemphigoid and anti-laminin 332 mucous membrane pemphigoid, so the serration pattern or an antigen-specific assay is still needed
options.rationale: Correct. The split side narrows the group rather than naming the disease; a u-serrated pattern is unique to type VII collagen.

options.text: Epidermal-side binding is diagnostic of bullous pemphigoid and excludes every other pemphigoid disease
options.rationale: Incorrect. Roof binders also include linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis and anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid.

options.text: Salt-split skin adds nothing, because direct immunofluorescence already named both diseases
options.rationale: Incorrect. Linear IgG/C3 is shared across the pemphigoid group, which is why direct immunofluorescence was only about 94% specific for bullous pemphigoid in one large series.

options.text: A negative type VII collagen ELISA in patient B excludes epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
options.rationale: Incorrect. That ELISA is only about 45% sensitive (about 50% combined with salt-split skin), so about half of these patients are seronegative.

questions.stem: A patient brings a commercial panel reporting IgG4 antibodies to 40 foods and asks which of them she is allergic to. The best response is that:

options.text: Food-specific IgG and IgG4 testing has no role in diagnosing adverse food reactions, because these antibodies are found in essentially all healthy people
options.rationale: Correct. Diagnosis rests on the clinical history with specific IgE or skin-prick testing and, when needed, oral food challenge.

options.text: The foods with the highest IgG4 levels should be eliminated first
options.rationale: Incorrect. Studies supporting IgG-guided diets had major methodological problems, and IgG to food is a normal response to what is eaten.

options.text: IgG4 to a food proves tolerance has been lost
options.rationale: Incorrect. If anything, food-specific IgG4 has been associated with tolerance, not with clinical allergy.

options.text: A positive specific IgE result on its own would have confirmed allergy instead
options.rationale: Incorrect. Specific IgE at the usual 0.35 kU/L cutoff is sensitive but poorly specific, so a positive result shows sensitisation and must be read with the clinical history.

references.citation: Patterson MF, Dorris SL. Food Allergy: Unproven diagnostics and therapeutics. J Food Allergy. 2020;2(1):91-94. doi:10.2500/jfa.2020.2.200013

claims.text: Pemphigus = intraepidermal acantholysis against desmoglein 1 and 3, suprabasal row of tombstones in pemphigus vulgaris, subcorneal split with mucosa spared in pemphigus foliaceus; pemphigoid = subepidermal split against BP180/collagen XVII and BP230.
Nikolsky sign positive in pemphigus (highly specific, moderately sensitive) and negative in bullous pemphigoid, which presents with tense blisters mainly at ages 75–80.
claims.note: Sensitivity qualification recorded as register flag rv-nikolsky-sensitivity.

claims.text: DIF on perilesional skin is the gold standard: intercellular IgG/C3 in pemphigus, linear IgG/C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction in pemphigoid diseases; the linear band is shared, and DIF was 78.1% sensitive and 93.6% specific for bullous pemphigoid in a 569-patient series.

On 1 mol/L NaCl split skin, roof (epidermal) binders target BP180/BP230 (bullous pemphigoid, linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis, anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid) and floor (dermal) binders include type VII collagen (epidermolysis bullosa acquisita), anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 and anti-laminin 332; u-serration is unique to type VII collagen.
claims.note: Roof/floor over-specificity recorded as register flag rv-salt-split-roof-floor.

claims.text: Salt-split indirect immunofluorescence 97.6% sensitive and 99.8% specific and BP180 NC16A ELISA 93.9% sensitive and 95.6% specific for bullous pemphigoid; desmoglein ELISA positive in more than 90% of pemphigus; COL7 ELISA about 45% sensitive and about 50% with split skin.

Food-specific IgG and IgG4 panels have no role in diagnosing adverse food reactions; IgG to foods occurs in essentially all healthy people; diagnosis rests on history with specific IgE or skin-prick testing and oral food challenge, and a positive specific IgE shows sensitisation rather than disease.
claims.note: The one narrow exception (Heiner syndrome) is recorded as register flag rv-igg4-food-heiner.

“Pemphigus peels, pemphigoid persists; BP rides the roof, EBA sinks to the floor.”

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 55 Hit 6 says salt-split skin “settles” bullous pemphigoid versus epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Witte 2018 lists several roof binders (bullous pemphigoid, linear IgA disease, pemphigoid gestationis, anti-BP180 mucous membrane pemphigoid) and several floor binders (epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, anti-p200/anti-laminin gamma-1 pemphigoid, anti-laminin 332 mucous membrane pemphigoid), so the split side narrows the group and serration pattern or antigen-specific assays are needed to name the disease (register flag rv-salt-split-roof-floor).

Ch. 55 Hit 5 states “Nikolsky POSITIVE” for pemphigus without qualification. Witte 2018 reports the sign is only moderately sensitive although highly specific, so a negative sign does not exclude pemphigus (register flag rv-nikolsky-sensitivity).

Ch. 55 Trap 6 says IgG4 to foods has no predictive value for clinical allergy. Patterson 2020 agrees there is no role in diagnosing adverse food reactions but notes one rare exception, food-induced pulmonary haemosiderosis (Heiner syndrome), and leaves the role in gastrointestinal disorders unsettled (register flag rv-igg4-food-heiner).
